chapters.1.lds: The lesson asks readers to examine attitudes and conduct condemned in the opening warning. What assumption does God’s searching lamp expose?
chapters.1.summary: The LORD’s word comes to Zephaniah in the days of King Josiah. God will sweep everything from the face of the earth. He will strike Judah and those who worship Baal and the stars. Some swear by the LORD and also by another god. The day of the LORD is near. He will search Jerusalem with lamps. He will punish those who say he does nothing, good or bad. It will be a day of wrath, and silver and gold will not save.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson contrasts pride with seeking humility before God. Why does possible shelter remain uncertain even for those who seek humility?
chapters.2.summary: Zephaniah calls the nation to gather before the day of anger comes. The humble of the land should seek the LORD. They should seek righteousness and humility. Perhaps they will be sheltered on that day. Philistia’s cities will be emptied. Moab and Ammon will become like Sodom for their pride. Ethiopia will fall by the sword. Nineveh, which said no one was like it, will become a home for wild animals.
chapters.3.lds: The lesson connects the promised joy with a later scene in 3 Nephi 17. How do the gathered people differ from the earlier city’s rulers?
chapters.3.summary: Zephaniah cries woe to the rebellious city that listens to no one. Its officials are roaring lions, and its judges are wolves. Its prophets are reckless, and its priests profane what is holy. The LORD within it does no wrong and gives justice every morning. He will purify the speech of the nations to call on his name. He will leave a humble and lowly people in the city. Zion is told to sing, for the LORD is among them. He will save the lame and gather the outcasts.
